questions.passage: The train stopped and the people got off.
questions.markingGuide: Accept any answer that places the train at a station/platform (e.g. 'at a station', 'at the train station', 'at a stop'). The clue is 'stopped' + 'people got off', which only happens at a station/platform. Reject answers describing an unrelated location (a house, shop, zoo, etc.) or answers that do not address where the train was.

questions.passage: Emma could see at least twenty large passenger jets from all over the world.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'at an/the airport' or equivalent (e.g. 'watching planes at the airport', 'at the airport terminal'). The clue is seeing many large passenger jets 'from all over the world', which only happens at an airport. Reject vague answers like 'outside' with no airport reference, or answers unrelated to planes/airports.

questions.passage: The tiger looked out through the bars.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'at the zoo', 'in a cage', 'in an enclosure', or 'in captivity'. The clue is 'bars', which the tiger is looking out 'through' (i.e. it is enclosed). Reject 'in the jungle/wild' or any answer that ignores the bars detail.

questions.prompt: Did she know it was wool when she first saw it? How do you know that?
questions.passage: As Tara got nearer to the barbed wire fence she could see that it was only a piece of dirty wool that was stuck on it.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'No' with evidence that she only recognised it as wool once she got closer/nearer (e.g. 'no, because it says as she got nearer she could see it was wool', 'no, she didn't know until she was close'). The word 'nearer...could see' implies she couldn't tell what it was from a distance. Reject 'yes' or a bare 'no' with no supporting reason from the text.

questions.prompt: Did the first two roads that were crossed have crossings or lights? How do you know that?
questions.passage: To get to school each day, I had to cross three roads. The third road had a crossing and lights so it was the safest one.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'No' with evidence referencing that only the third road is described as having a crossing and lights, and is called 'the safest one' (implying the other two were less safe, i.e. without crossings/lights). E.g. 'no, because only the third road had them and it says that one was the safest'. Reject 'yes' or an unsupported 'no'.

questions.prompt: What time of day was it?
questions.passage:
As he walked up the path Kim was surprised to see that there was not a light anywhere, not even the flicker of the TV. He also noticed how unusually quiet it was. Toby didn't let anyone get anywhere near the house without yapping 'or growling.

Slowly Kim opened the front door and peered into the silence. "Is there ... anybody home?" he called in a shaky voice. But there was no reply. He called again, his voice a little stronger this time. Still silence.

He went slowly into the hallway, his fingers reaching for the light switch on the wall. As soon as he pushed the switch Kim realised the power in the house was off. He stood for a while, until his eyes were used to the dark. He wondered why no-one was home. No parents, no little sister, not even Toby.

He made his way to the kitchen. He could 'see' every step of the way in his mind. Ever since he had been very little, Kim had often got up for a drink in the middle of the night and padded in darkness to the fridge.

The torch was in its usual place, although Kim opened the wrong drawer at first He immediately shone the torch on the kitchen table. He breathed a sigh of relief as he read the note - 'Have gone to the vet, we shouldn't be too long'.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'night' or 'evening/dark' — supported by 'not a light anywhere', needing a torch, and eyes adjusting 'to the dark'. Reject 'daytime/morning/afternoon'.
